scope: Proposition 7.1 (Class division) of the manuscript “Deterministic Polynomial Factorization over Prime Fields” (preprints/Deterministic-Polynomial-Factorization-over-Prime-Fields-October-4-2026/Deterministic-Polynomial-Factorization-over-Prime-Fields.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 142 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ed88aa5ba802311a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 33. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let k, q, F, C, and σ be as in Proposition 5.1, and suppose the auxiliary primary-group data required by Theorem 6.1 are available. Let P = (x, 0) be a specified k-rational ramification point. Given a represented degree-zero divisor D satisfying char k > (N + 2∥D∥ + 1)2, under the promise that [D] ∈ (1 − σ) Pic0 (C)(k), there is a deterministic procedure LambdaDivide(D, P) returning a degree-zero divisor D′ with ∥D′ ∥ ≤ 2g, (1 − σ)[D′ ] = [D]. It uses polynomially many field operations in the representation size, q, N, ∥D∥, and log |k|, with the uniform norm bound from Theorem 6.1. It is compatible with simultaneous execution over the algebra of the unknown roots of F.
